# Package validation

These checks target Unity 2022.3 and VRChat Avatars SDK 3.10.x. They test the standalone package without the original Gesture Manager installed.

## Static checks

Run `node .github/scripts/Validate-Package.cjs` with `--dependency-root` pointing to each installed `com.vrchat.base` and `com.vrchat.avatars` package. To also check coexistence GUID isolation against an original Gesture Manager checkout, pass `--original-root` with that checkout's path.

The validator checks assembly dependencies, asset metadata, GUID uniqueness, serialized references, resource lookups, and the native DLL hash/importer/license files. Missing historical references are reported separately when an original baseline is available; they are not counted as resolved.

`node .github/scripts/Prune-ControllerOrphans.cjs` performs a dry run of controller graph reachability. `--apply` prunes orphan object blocks in the eight built-in controllers and their matching restore snapshots. It verifies that the retained objects are byte-for-byte unchanged and rejects missing local graph references. This cleanup was applied to the initial Pro baseline after checking that other package assets and source code did not reference the orphan subobjects.

For a read-only report of external controller references, run `node .github/scripts/Inspect-ControllerReferences.cjs --sdk-root <com.vrchat.avatars directory>`. Supply `--output <report.json>` only when a saved diagnostic report is needed.

## Unity integration checks

Use a disposable Unity avatar project with the target SDK and this package installed. Copy `UnityProChecks.cs`, `UnityProMotionChecks.cs`, `UnityProPlayChecks.cs`, `UnityProGraphChecks.cs`, `UnityProCameraChecks.cs`, `UnityProSimulationRenderChecks.cs`, `UnityProStatisticsChecks.cs`, `UnityProStatisticsLifecycleChecks.cs`, `UnityProFontChecks.cs`, and `UnityProValidation.asmdef` into its `Assets/Editor` folder. Do not copy these scripts into a user's working avatar project for batch testing.

Run Unity with `-batchmode -nographics -projectPath <fixture> -executeMethod UnityProChecks.Run -logFile <log>`. For actual Play Mode session checks and GPU-rendered camera images, use a second invocation with `-executeMethod UnityProPlayChecks.Run` and omit `-nographics`. These runners exit Unity themselves; do not add `-quit` to the Play runner. Rendered validation images are saved beneath the fixture's `Temp/GestureManagerProValidation/SimulationViews` folder.

The editor runner creates a temporary GUI context to check localized UI caches, resource ownership, native analyzer initialization and preservation of user names/parameter identities. It also checks standard tool registration across the feature assemblies, explicit manager binding, defaults, radial-first initialization, shared radial/Inspector sessions, radial icons, live localized tool captions and the absence of standalone feature menus or a language Preferences page. The motion checks inject deterministic input. Play checks exercise session ownership, movement publication, stop/pause/unlink/failure cleanup and restoration. The graph checks initialize a valid generic avatar through the actual simulator connection path and eight default animation layers. They do not automate physical key presses, microphone hardware, VR hardware, humanoid body IK or visual layout inspection.

The GitHub workflow builds an archive only. It does not replace Unity integration or hardware validation.

`UnityProFontChecks` opens Model Statistics and two independent fixture windows together and checks their shared language-specific font chains, synthetic weight configuration, language switching and root attachment cleanup. The runtime tools use the inherited IMGUI theme. The font check generates a real multi-page CJK atlas with unused null capacity, checks resource stability over 200 updates, and verifies recovery after invalidating an owned material or active atlas page. Actual scrolling/window geometry, glyph rendering and Play Mode font transitions still require graphics-enabled checks; the synchronous editor assertions do not replace those checks.

The statistics checks compare all 31 metric values and PC/Mobile grades with the installed SDK calculator, including simulator components, complete Bounds, raw constraint depth, available size values and unknown-value ratings. They check component/asset state, SDK ignore-delegate preservation, separate before-processing and processed records, the 48-record session history, avatar identity filtering, stage selection and localized UI. Injected SDK event payloads test build-state correlation, actual build-platform identification and bundle-size reporting for the matching platform only; these are not a real SDK build or external-processor acceptance test. Play Mode observations use the first Editor update, while manual Play Mode scans remain a separate source.

Run `UnityProChecks.Run` once more without `-nographics` to exercise the non-readable help-icon regression. It discards a test texture's CPU pixels, copies it through the production helper, compares GPU-rendered color/alpha pixels, checks error logs and verifies source/render-target preservation. The headless invocation explicitly skips that GPU-only check.

The Play runner also creates an unsaved avatar in the disposable fixture and runs the real SDK preprocessing callback pipeline on entering Play Mode. A controlled test processor removes one cube: both platform histories must retain 24 triangles before processing and 12 afterwards, independently of simulator initialization. This tests callback timing, not NDMF, MA or AAO compatibility. An optional fixture-only APW reference DLL can expose the upstream `AvatarPerformanceInfo`, `PerformanceInfo` and `PerformanceRankComputer` unchanged inside `ReadOnlyStatsComparison.ApwAlgorithm`, preserving the upstream MIT notice. The runner compares all metrics and overall ratings against that calculator by reflection. Add `-apwReferenceRequired` to fail if the reference is absent; otherwise this comparison explicitly reports a skip. Do not include APW's window or preprocessing callback in the reference DLL, and do not distribute it with Pro.
